# Routing Decisions — IMF 2022 Article IV (MAC-010), Pages 51–60

## High-Recall Context (applies to all chunks)

All ten chunks consist of IMF statistical tables, an External Sector Assessment annex, a Risk Assessment Matrix, and a Debt Sustainability Analysis. These are technical/statistical annex pages with the page-1 cover and main narrative already excluded from this batch. The role of the IMF source for 5B is high — the document records concrete measurable outcomes (fiscal balance, debt path, inflation, growth, financial soundness, reserves adequacy, structural-reform priorities, and policy-reaction functions under shocks) attributable to Mexico's rulers in 2021–2022. Adjacent narrative needed to interpret the tables has already been routed from earlier batches; these pages are the data spine.

The exclusion threshold is met only by chunks lacking any concrete named policy, measurable outcome, cost, distributional result, implementation finding, attributed action, or contrary finding tied to ruler action. Tables of pure historical outturn numbers without a policy attribution, method qualifier, or qualifying IMF assessment are usually non-material as standalone evidence for 5B; but the DSA, External Sector Assessment, and Risk Assessment Matrix pages go beyond pure numbers and contain named qualifications, attributed policy responses, structural-reform priorities, and contrary findings about the fiscal stance — they are included.

---

## Decision Table

| chunk_id | decision | question_ids | relevance | adjacent_context_needed | exclusion_reason_if_excluded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U0051 | INCLUDE | 5B.10, 5B.9 | Material measures: projected current-account deficit (–1.2% to –0.9% of GDP 2022–2027); FDI net of –1.9 to –2.6% of GDP; reserves adequacy trajectory; merchandise trade balance; remittances 3.8–3.9% of GDP; primary-income deficit persistent at –2.2 to –3.3% of GDP. Supplies external-balance measurements for shock-response and trajectory assessments. | For 5B.10, the matched earlier staff narrative on the investment-savings gap and fiscal stance that anchors interpretation of these balances. U0051 provides the measured outcome those narratives assert. | — |
| U0052 | INCLUDE | 5B.10, 5B.9 | Same balance-of-payments series as U0051 but in %-of-GDP terms, enabling distributional/comparative reading across years. Primary-income outflows, remittance inflows, and external-debt ratios are directly relevant to incidence (who bears adjustment) and to trajectory. | Same narrative as U0051; U0052 confirms the level normalization. | — |
| U0053 | INCLUDE | 5B.3, 5B.6 | Concrete measured outcomes for prudential and financial-rule compliance: capital-adequacy ratio 14.9→18.7% (2016–2022Q2); NPL ratio 2.0–2.4%; ROE 11.7–20.9%; liquid-assets/short-term-liabilities 31.1–38.5%. Supplies hard evidence the financial-rules regime held under the ruler's term and that banking-sector institutions delivered stability — addresses 5B.3 (credible financial rules protecting stability). | The staff assessment of banking-system resilience (drawn from financial-sector narrative pages already routed). U0053 is the numeric spine. | — |
| U0054 | INCLUDE | 5B.3, 5B.9, 5B.10 | Concrete measured outcomes: 28-day treasury rate 4.4–7.8%; EMBIG spread 318–474 bps; 10-year local-currency yield 6.3–8.4%; gross international reserves US$183–207.7 bn; gross external debt 31.6–42.6% of GDP; reserves adequacy 116.2–131.2% of ARA metric; gross financing needs US$76–102 bn. Directly material to monetary/debt-rule credibility and to shock-resilience readings. | The earlier staff commentary on the floating regime and reserve adequacy. U0054 supplies the numbers behind those assessments. | — |
| U0055 | INCLUDE | 5B.6, 5B.9, 5B.10 | Concrete measured outcomes and a contrary finding: GDP growth 2.1% (2022) → 1.2% (2023) → 1.8% (2024) → 2.1% (2027); non-financial public sector overall balance –2.3% (2019) to –4.4% (2020) to –3.8% (2021–2022) to –4.1% (2023); primary balance +0.7 → +0.3 → +1.8 → +1.6; consumer-price inflation average 8.0% (2022) → 6.3% (2023) → 3.0% (2027); gross fixed investment ~21% of GDP; terms-of-trade improvement 3.0 (2023). The headline fiscal balance shows a deterioration rather than a stabilization, and investment composition skews to private — both are substantive contrary/distributional findings for 5B.10 and 5B.9. | The earlier staff narrative on fiscal-stance tightening and the balanced-budget-rule impact; U0055 measures the trajectory those pages assert. | — |
| U0056 | INCLUDE | 5B.3, 5B.9 | Concrete measured outcomes for monetary regime compliance: monetary-base growth 8.3%→21.6%→11.0%; broad-money growth 4.5%→13.4%→11.0%; bank credit to non-financial private sector 26.8%→26.5% of GDP; net credit to public sector via Banco de México; currency-in-circulation growth 8.9%→11.0%. Supplies the data behind any monetary-discipline assessment. | Earlier narrative on Banco de México's inflation-targeting response; U0056 is the numeric spine. | — |
| U0057 | INCLUDE | 5B.1, 5B.2, 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10 | Highest-density evidence page in the batch (External Sector Assessment). Named structural-reform priorities: informality, governance gaps, private participation in energy, Pemex business strategy and governance. Policy recommendations on floating exchange rate, FX intervention only to prevent disorderly conditions, and continued Flexible Credit Line use. Concrete measured outcomes: NIIP –41% → –35% of GDP; FDI 18% of GDP; reserves 16% of GDP; gross public external debt 23% of GDP with ~25% in local currency; CA deficit –0.4% of GDP (2021) projected to –1.2% (2023) and to stabilize at –1% medium term; cyclically adjusted CA norm –1.2% (staff gap –0.2%); REER appreciation ~6% (2021) and 3% (mid-2022); reserves 131% of ARA, 254% of short-term debt (by remaining maturity). Contrary/distributional findings: domestic fuel price ceiling and fuel subsidies amplify CA weakness from oil-price pass-through; relatively accommodative fiscal stances of trading partners drive a 1.2-pp fiscal-gap contribution to EBA model; NIIP vulnerability to gross foreign portfolio liabilities. 5B.7 is touched via IMF-staff adjustments for transitory COVID impact — an explicit acknowledgement of independent evaluation. | None beyond the corpus already routed; this page stands on its own. | — |
| U0058 | INCLUDE | 5B.9 | Risk Assessment Matrix with named concrete policy responses under defined shocks: (i) commodity-price shocks → monetary policy should respond if shocks feed into core inflation and anchor expectations; (ii) systemic social unrest → tighten monetary policy + increase and better target social transfers to vulnerable households + accelerate investment in low-income regions; (iii) de-anchoring of inflation expectations and stagflation → monetary policy should respond decisively to keep the policy rate contractionary; (iv) abrupt global slowdown or U.S. recession → tighten monetary policy if inflation is affected but decouple from the Fed when appropriate, frontload fiscal expenditure, delay revenue measures. Each risk row has a likelihood rating and contains a contrary/distributional finding (e.g., "preserving fossil-fuel subsidies" as a damaging populist policy). Material for 5B.9 (timely, funded, transparently targeted measures under shocks) and 5B.8 (regional targeting of social transfers). | The earlier RAM-introduction narrative; U0058 supplies the policy-response matrix proper. | — |
| U0059 | INCLUDE | 5B.9, 5B.4, 5B.6 | Continued Risk Assessment Matrix: (i) local COVID-19 outbreaks → renew vaccination campaign, seek variant-matched boosters, consider renewing pandemic-era support for key industries, expand targeting of transfers to protect the most vulnerable; (ii) deepening geo-economic fragmentation → implement structural reforms so the economy can adjust flexibly to rotation in export demand, including labor-market reforms to reduce informality. Concrete attributed policy actions ("renew," "implement," "accelerate") tied to a contrary reading (fragmentation) are material. The "reduce informality" structural-reform call matches the 5B.4 fair-competition and property lens and 5B.6 administrative-capacity lens. | Earlier RAM page U0058 for context; this page continues it. | — |
| U0060 | INCLUDE | 5B.3, 5B.6, 5B.7, 5B.10 | Debt Sustainability Assessment with concrete contrary findings and qualifications: overall risk of sovereign stress = Moderate; medium-term assessment = Moderate (Fanchart suggests non-stabilization of debt by end of projection; GFN analysis indicates financing needs broadly stable; standardized stress tests suggest additional GFN could reach ~15% of GDP in stress scenarios); long-term = Moderate (restrictive fiscal stance + absence of structural reforms creates a trade-off between long-run growth and budget balance, so debt ratios may not achieve a declining trend); sustainability = sustainable with high probability but notable risks from further shocks. Explicit qualifications on the balanced-budget rule — "the impact on budget composition could be a long-run issue as expenditures on investment and developmental objectives are often restrained to ensure compliance" — is a directly material contrary finding for 5B.6 (timely, high-quality infrastructure rather than announcements) and for 5B.7 (correcting laws/programs when evidence shows failure, here the IMF staff explicitly flags a structural-rule weakness). | Earlier DSA-narrative pages; U0060 is the matrix/qualification page. | — |

## Routing Summary

- Included: 10 / 10
- Excluded: 0 / 0
- Pages 51–60 of the IMF 2022 Article IV are uniformly evidence-bearing for Chapter 5B. Every page carries concrete measured outcomes (fiscal balance, debt path, inflation, growth, financial soundness, reserves adequacy) and pages 57–60 additionally carry IMF-staff qualifications, contrary findings, and named attributed policy recommendations under shock scenarios. No page in this batch is purely definitional, generic background, or reference material.
